The alarm was installed in April 2019 with a 7-year lifespan, putting end-of-life at April 2026 — it's already about six months past that. Since it's a sealed unit, the tenant can't just swap the battery; the chirping is the end-of-life signal, not an active CO detection, but an expired alarm is unreliable enough that I'd treat this as urgent and recommend replacement within 72 hours while advising the tenant not to tamper with the sealed unit.

This is clearly the landlord's responsibility — sealed battery units aren't tenant-replaceable, so the usual rule doesn't apply, and landlords are legally obligated to maintain a working CO alarm. arguments.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Please don't remove or cover the alarm. Its battery is sealed, and a once-a-minute chirp usually means it has reached the end of its life (it was fitted in 2019), so it needs replacing rather than a new battery. Until then, please don't rely on it. If it ever sounds continuously, or anyone feels dizzy, has a headache, nausea or feels drowsy, leave the flat, call the National Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999 (or 999 if someone is unwell) and tell us. Please also keep a window open a little. We're asking your landlord to approve a replacement and aim to get it done within 72 hours. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan as a routine job. You'll hear from us by Monday 12 Oct.

This is clearly the landlord's responsibility — sealed battery units aren't tenant-replaceable, so the usual rule doesn't apply, and landlords are legally obligated to maintain a working CO alarm. Replacement is cheap and well within the £300 spend limit, so I should check for any existing tickets and property details, and since I can't call back after the dropped call, I'll follow up with an SMS instead.

answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan); asked Ben for approval (APR-104); scheduled follow-up FUP-105 for 12 Oct; texted the tenant not to remove or cover the alarm, to ventilate, to leave and call 0800 111 999/999 if the alarm goes continuous or anyone has symptoms, with a 72h target and next update by 12 Oct.

conflicts: Caller asked to remove the battery, but the record says sealed battery, so that isn't possible or advisable.
assumptions: Chirp pattern indicates end-of-life; cannot be verified remotely.
The call dropped before the tenant got an answer, so SMS was used.
